title.en: Timber grain across long faces and cut ends

summary: Keep grain tied to the timber member and distinguish a crosscut end from a longitudinal face.
objective: Make exposed timber ends and side faces read as parts cut from the same piece.
intent_signals: Make exposed timber ends and side faces read as parts cut from the same piece.
example_prompts: Build a timber footbridge whose cut post ends and long rails have coherent grain, without specifying a wood species.

principles: Treat a solid member as one oriented piece: face patterns should agree with its assigned fiber axis and cuts. Veneers, laminates and painted wood can have different authored layer boundaries.
Separate cut anatomy from finish. A varnish or paint treatment does not choose the grain direction, strength or contact friction.
implementation: Assign a local grain axis before unwrapping; use distinct crosscut and longitudinal coordinates at exposed ends instead of projecting the same stripe image onto every face. For a named species, research the particular visible pattern.

Give rails, tenons and cut ends actual thickness. Use geometry for silhouette-changing splits or chipped corners, and small-scale shading detail for unresolved fibers; keep the grain scale consistent between adjacent members.
Compare a sanded face and an intentionally rough end under one broad light at both hero and overview distances. Vary finish independently of grain color; avoid making every grain line a deep groove.
observable_checks: Orbit an exposed beam corner: end pattern changes with the cut while lengthwise grain follows the member rather than world axes.
Resize one member: check that texture scale does not silently turn fine grain into wide stripes or align unrelated cuts identically.
Disable normal detail and inspect the silhouette; a modeled split stays open, while a surface mark need not.

known_limits: This is not species identification, moisture response, anisotropic strength or a friction model.
Authored modeling and inspection guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Painted, flat-shaded or exaggerated grain can retain the cut distinction without photorealistic texture.
A fictional laminated beam may intentionally expose alternating directions if the layer construction is clear.

claims.statement: The Wood Handbook distinguishes transverse cross sections from radial and tangential longitudinal sections; cutting a board across the grain exposes a transverse section.
claims.scope: Wood anatomical section orientation only; no prescribed grain graphic or material property.

source_refs.locator: Printed page 3-4 (PDF page index 3), Planes of Section, paragraphs 1-4
